title: Finite symmetric tensor categories and the Verlinde tower
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: The proof, after OpenAI's 2026 manuscript, of the finite case of the Benson-Etingof-Ostrik conjecture: every finite symmetric tensor category over an algebraically closed field of characteristic p > 0 admits a fibre functor to a higher Verlinde category Ver_{p^n}, including p = 2. Finite symmetric tensor categories, Deligne products and dimensions; rational SL_2-modules and tilting modules; an equivariant vector bundle on the plane and the restricted tilting theorem (a conjecture of Coulembier and Flake); higher Frobenius functors; norm maps, Chouinard's theorem and total symmetrizers; rank varieties and a Moore-determinant choice of embedding; descent through Frobenius-Perron dimensions; incompressible categories, uniqueness in characteristic two and reconstruction over a higher Verlinde category.
prerequisites: rigid symmetric tensor categories, fibre functors and neutral Tannakian reconstruction (course The affine Grassmannian and geometric Satake, GL-SAT-09 Tannakian categories)
representations of sl(2) in characteristic zero, for comparison (course Semisimple Lie algebras, RT-LIE-05)
representations of finite groups, induced representations and Frobenius reciprocity (course Representations of finite groups)
finite-dimensional algebras and modules, the Jacobson radical, Nakayama's lemma
coherent sheaves and vector bundles on varieties, duals of coherent sheaves

open_obligations: N1 The higher Verlinde categories of Benson, Etingof and Ostrik (arXiv:2003.10499v4): construction as abelian envelopes of quotients of tilting modules, the fully faithful functor from T/I_n (Theorem 4.2), the tower inclusions (Theorem 4.34), definition over F_p (Section 4.9), the low levels and Ver_4^+ (Theorem 4.5, Corollary 4.11), the tensor subcategories (Corollary 4.61) and incompressibility (Theorem 4.71, Remark 4.72; Benson-Etingof Theorem 4.4). Stated in lesson 1, Theorem 4.2, and lesson 9, Theorem 1.1. Intended home: a course on symmetric tensor categories in positive characteristic (ALG-TENSOR in the building list).

N2 Finite tensor categories (EGNO): Deligne products, the Frobenius-Perron dimension, categorical traces and dimensions in symmetric categories, projectives tensored with objects, images of exact functors and the inequalities for FPdim(C). Stated in lesson 1, Theorems 2.1, 3.1, 3.3, lesson 5, Proposition 5.1, and lesson 9, Theorem 1.1. Intended home: the same course.

N3 Rational representations of SL_2 in characteristic p: classification of simple modules and Steinberg's tensor product theorem (Steinberg 1963; Riche, Chapter 1), Ext vanishing between Weyl and costandard modules, the Ext criteria for filtrations and indecomposable tilting modules (Riche, Chapter 1, Proposition 2.6; Chapter 4, Proposition 1.1 and Theorem 1.5), Donkin's formula for St_1 (Riche, Chapter 4, Proposition 1.15). Stated in lesson 2, Theorems 2.1, 3.1, 4.2. Intended home: a course on modular representations of reductive groups.

N4 Reflexive coherent sheaves (Stacks Project, Lemmas 28.23.5, 31.13.8, 31.13.12, 31.13.15). Stated in lesson 3, Theorem 3.1. Intended home: the algebraic geometry courses built on the AI-integrated Stacks project.
N5 The higher Frobenius construction of Coulembier and Flake (arXiv:2405.19506v2, Theorems 5.3.5, 5.4.3, 5.2.1, Proposition 3.2.6). Stated in lesson 5, Theorem 2.1. Intended home: ALG-TENSOR.

N6 Chouinard's theorem, Dade's lemma and the tensor product theorem for rank varieties (Benson, LNM 1081, Corollary 2.24.5, Corollary 2.25.8, Theorems 2.25.7 and 2.26.9). Stated in lesson 6, Theorem 2.1, and lesson 7, Theorem 1.2. Intended home: a course on modular representation theory of finite groups.

N7 Kleshchev's faithfulness theorem for the projective cover of the trivial module of S_m (Coulembier-Etingof-Ostrik, arXiv:2107.02372v2, Proposition A.1); the symmetrizer lemma is proved from it in lesson 6, Lemma 2.3. Intended home: the symmetric group lessons of the course Representations of finite groups.
N8 The Frobenius functor of Etingof and Ostrik (arXiv:1912.12947v2: Proposition 6.3, Proposition 7.4, Theorem 8.1, Corollary 9.5). Stated in lesson 8, Theorem 1.1. Intended home: ALG-TENSOR.
N9 The extension theorem of Etingof and Gelaki in characteristic two (arXiv:1904.07576v2, Theorem 2.21(2)). Stated in lesson 8, Theorem 1.2. Intended home: ALG-TENSOR.

N10 Subterminality of Ver_{2^infinity} and generalized Tannaka reconstruction (Coulembier-Etingof-Ostrik, arXiv:2306.09745v1, Theorems 9.4.1 and 4.2.1). Stated in lesson 9, Theorem 1.2. Intended home: ALG-TENSOR.
